I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

The caller passes resolved PR values, so I follow `reference/pr-head.md` in place of Steps 0 and 1. All commands run from the process cwd, which never changes. Every git command targets a repo with `-C`.

## Resolve ROOT and home

1. `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir` → both `/work/widget/.git`, so GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON.
2. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree` → empty, so this is not a submodule.
3. Resolved values:
   - **ROOT** = `/work/widget`, which matches the caller.
   - **Overrides:** none affect creation (no `home:`, `create:` or wrapper). The file-scoped runner matters only for conflicts.
   - **Home:** `headRefName` = `fix/retry`, so `<name>` = `fix-retry` and **WORKTREE** = `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
   - **MEMBER_HEADS**, in order: #13 `fix/cap` @ `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, then #14 `fix/retry-docs` @ `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`.

## Fetch and pre-write checks (nothing written yet)

4. `git -C /work/widget fetch origin` → succeeds.
5. Check that each original head exists and that its remote branch equals it:
   - #12:
     - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}` → ok
     - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry` → `aaaa…aaaa`, which equals the supplied head
   - #13:
     - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}` → ok
     - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap` → `bbbb…bbbb`, equal
   - #14:
     - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}` → ok
     - `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs` → `cccc…cccc`, equal
6. `git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main` → **BASE_SHA** = `dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd`.
7. Ordered stops:
   - **Fork-hosted:** `isCrossRepository` is false for all three. Pass.
   - **Branch checked out elsewhere:** `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain` lists only the primary. Pass.
   - **Reachability:** passed in step 5.
   - **Local branch ancestry:** there is no local `fix/retry`, so this check does not apply.
8. **Interrupted-merge recovery:** there is no existing home worktree or local branch, so recovery is skipped.

**If #14 were unreachable or had moved:** step 5 would stop with `PR #14 head ccccccc is not reachable (origin/fix/retry-docs is at <sha7>); the branch moved.` That stop comes after the fetch and before any write. No worktree, no `worktree add`, no checkout of `fix/retry`, and no merge of #13 would happen.

## Provision the exact head

9. Clean-base check: `git -C /work/widget status --porcelain` exits 0 with empty output, so the base is clean.
10. Home is inside ROOT, so check that it is gitignored: `git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees` → exit 0. It is already ignored, so no `.gitignore` commit is needed.
11. State matches "no worktree, no local branch". Run `git -C /work/widget worktree add "/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry" fix/retry`. Unique-remote DWIM tracks `origin/fix/retry`.
12. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` → `aaaa…aaaa`, which equals `headRefOid`.
13. Captured values:
    - **PRE_REWORK_HEAD** = `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
    - **BASE_SHA** = `dddd…dddd`
14. No provenance note is added, because the base is the PR head itself.

## Member merges, in listed order

15. Merge #13:
    - Last-good SHA: `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` → `aaaa…aaaa`
    - `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12" bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` → clean, producing `eeeeeee`
16. Merge #14:
    - Last-good SHA: `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD` → `eeeeeee…`
    - `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12" cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc` → clean, producing `fffffff`

There were no conflicts, so no helper was dispatched and no scoped tests ran.

## Base merge

17. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main` → clean, producing `1111111`.

## All-head ancestry proofs against final HEAD

18. Each command exits 0, so all three original heads are preserved:
    - `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa HEAD`
    - `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb HEAD`
    - `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc HEAD`

## Read-back

19. `git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain` → includes `worktree /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`.
20. `git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry branch --show-current` → `fix/retry`. Both read-backs match.

Nothing was rebased, reset or amended at or below PRE_REWORK_HEAD. Nothing was pushed or closed, and no spec or plan was written. Next, the review-thread fetch runs per PR (#12, #13, #14) before gather. MEMBER_HEADS are carried forward to gather.

## Step 4 report

```
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa (clean)
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Member merge: #13 eeeeeee
Member merge: #14 fffffff
merge: 1111111
Base SHA: ddddddd
Ready to implement retry-cap rework for #12 (with #13, #14)
```

I'm using the using-git-worktrees skill to set up an isolated workspace.

This is a synthetic narration; no tools are invoked. **Every command below runs with cwd `/work/widget`**, without changing the process cwd. Seven-character merge IDs denote the supplied commits; where a full ID is required, I retain that commit’s full object ID rather than inventing its unspecified suffix.

### 1. Resolve the PR-head workspace

The admitted order is home **#12**, then **#13**, then **#14**. All three are in-repository PRs targeting `main`.

Commands, in order:

```bash
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir --git-common-dir
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree
```

Resolve:

- `GIT_DIR = GIT_COMMON = /work/widget/.git`
- Superproject output: empty.
- `ROOT=/work/widget`; primary checkout, not a submodule.
- `BRANCH=fix/retry`
- `NAME=fix-retry`
- `WORKTREE=/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry`
- `PRE_REWORK_HEAD=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`
- Members, retained in order:
  - #13: `fix/cap`, `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`
  - #14: `fix/retry-docs`, `cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc`

Check the overrides ladder:

```bash
for p in .pi/gauntlet-overrides.md gauntlet-overrides.md doc/gauntlet-overrides.md; do if [ -f "/work/widget/$p" ]; then cat "/work/widget/$p"; break; fi; done
```

No overrides file is present. No native creation tool is available. Discover project instructions and wrappers:

```bash
if [ -f /work/widget/AGENTS.md ]; then cat /work/widget/AGENTS.md; fi
ls -la /work/widget /work/widget/script /work/widget/bin
```

No wrapper or alternative home applies. The selected home is the default home.

### 2. Fetch and finish all pre-write checks

```bash
git -C /work/widget fetch origin
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa^{commit}
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb^{commit}
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/cap
git -C /work/widget rev-parse --verify -q cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc^{commit}
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/fix/retry-docs
git -C /work/widget rev-parse origin/main
```

All original commit objects exist. Each remote head equals its supplied original head. Resolve:

```text
BASE_SHA=dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd
```

The metadata fork check passes for every PR. Continue:

```bash
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget branch --list fix/retry
test -e /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
```

There is no conflicting worktree, no local home branch, and the selected path is absent, as stipulated. No recovery or local-branch ancestry check is needed.

**The requested hypothetical failure boundary:** an unreachable or moved #14 stops at its object/remote validation above, before any checkout, ignore-file modification, or worktree creation:

```text
PR #14 head ccccccc is not reachable (origin/fix/retry-docs is at <observed sha7>); the branch moved.
```

That is not the outcome of this run; #14 passes.

### 3. Provision the exact home head

Setting up an isolated worktree at `/work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry` on branch `fix/retry` for this work.

```bash
git -C /work/widget status --porcelain
git -C /work/widget check-ignore -q .worktrees
```

The source is clean. The ignore check succeeds, so no `.gitignore` write or commit is needed.

```bash
git -C /work/widget worktree add /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry fix/retry
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widget worktree list --porcelain
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry branch --show-current
```

Unique-remote DWIM checks out the existing remote branch. HEAD equals the full original #12 head. Read-backs confirm the selected path and branch `fix/retry`.

### 4. Merge members, then fetched base

Save the last-good full home SHA, then merge #13’s original head:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #13 head bbbbbbb into PR #12" bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
```

Saved SHA: `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`. Clean merge: `eeeeeee`.

Save the new last-good full SHA, then merge #14’s original head:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff -m "merge PR #14 head ccccccc into PR #12" cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
```

Saved SHA: full object ID of `eeeeeee`. Clean merge: `fffffff`.

Now merge the fetched base:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge --no-ff --no-edit origin/main
```

Clean merge: `1111111`. No conflict helper or tests run.

Prove every original PR head remains an ancestor of final HEAD:

```bash
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb HEAD
git -C /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry merge-base --is-ancestor cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc HEAD
```

All three exit 0.

### Step 4 report

```text
Worktree ready at /work/widget/.worktrees/fix-retry
Branch: fix/retry
Base: fix/retry @ aaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#12
Pre-rework head: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
PR: acme/widget#13
Pre-rework head: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
PR: acme/widget#14
Pre-rework head: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
Base SHA: ddddddd
Member merge: #13 eeeeeee
Member merge: #14 fffffff
merge: 1111111
Ready to implement retry caps
```

Stop here: no gather, push, close, spec, or plan writes.
